title: useTabFeatures drops the fetch error; 12 headers show a failed load as 0/N
instrument: Component test per header: mock /api/feature-matrix?moduleId= to 500, render sub_combat index, assert the TabHeader shows an error/unknown state rather than implemented=0. Count headers that distinguish failure: before 0/12.
evidence:
src/hooks/useTabFeatures.ts:25 `const { features, isLoading } = useFeatureMatrix(moduleId);` (error discarded)
src/hooks/useTabFeatures.ts:34-44 stats counts every def as unknown when features=[]
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/index.tsx:74 `<TabHeader ... implemented={stats.implemented} total={stats.total}`
12 callers: grep -rn "useTabFeatures(" src/components (sub_ability, sub_animation, sub_bestiary, sub_character, sub_combat, sub_debug, sub_inventory, sub_loot, sub_progression, sub_save, sub_ui, sub_world)
body:
## Summary
useTabFeatures returns no error field, so every core-engine module header renders a failed feature-matrix fetch as a real "0 of N implemented" count.

## Description
src/hooks/useTabFeatures.ts:25 destructures only features/isLoading from useFeatureMatrix and drops `error`. On a failed GET, features stays [] and stats (src/hooks/useTabFeatures.ts:34) counts all defs as not implemented; the 12 sub_* headers (e.g. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/index.tsx:74) show 0/N as fact. async-ui-states/state-model: an error is not an empty state. Fixed = the hook exposes `error`/`retry` and headers render an unknown/failed state.

## Flow
- DB locked or API 500 on /api/feature-matrix?moduleId=arpg-combat
- useFeatureMatrix sets error, features=[]
- useTabFeatures discards error, stats.implemented=0
- Combat header reads "0/N implemented"

## Expected impact
Designers stop mistaking an outage for an unbuilt module. Touches 12 consumer files outside this context, so it needs an owning worker; risk: header layout for the new state.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - failed loads stop rendering as zero progress
Before: 0 of 12 module headers can distinguish failure from zero (walked sub_combat, sub_loot, sub_world)
After: predicted 12/12 with error exposed and rendered
Method: simulation - consumers are outside this round's paths, so no gate was run on them
Result: better
Gate: none

title: useGenreEvolution swallows load failures; panel shows the 0-scans empty state
instrument: Test: mockFetchRoutes /api/telemetry -> 500 for stats+history, render TelemetryEvolution, assert an error state (not EmptyState with scanCount 0). Before: EmptyState shown.
evidence:
src/hooks/useGenreEvolution.ts:39 `apiFetch<TelemetryStats>(...).catch(() => null)`
src/hooks/useGenreEvolution.ts:40 `.catch(() => [] as TelemetrySnapshot[])`
src/components/modules/core-engine/TelemetryEvolution/index.tsx:151 `<EmptyState ... scanCount={stats?.totalScans ?? 0} />`
body:
## Summary
fetchGenreData catches both telemetry reads into null/[] so a failed load is indistinguishable from a project that was never scanned.

## Description
src/hooks/useGenreEvolution.ts:39-40 convert any error to stats=null / history=[]; useCRUD then reports success. TelemetryEvolution (src/components/modules/core-engine/TelemetryEvolution/index.tsx:151) renders the EmptyState inviting a first scan. Fixed = the fetcher lets the error reach useCRUD (or returns a loadError) and the view renders an InlineErrorRetry.

## Flow
- /api/telemetry returns 500
- both reads are caught to null/[]
- useCRUD error stays null
- panel shows "0 scans - run your first scan"

## Expected impact
A user with scan history stops being told they have none. The view change lives in core-engine-scan-telemetry (outside this context).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - load failure surfaces as failure
Before: failed load -> EmptyState with scanCount 0 (read path walked)
After: predicted: error state with Retry
Method: simulation - the view that must render it is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Commit buffer drops a pending debounced edit when entityId changes unflushed
instrument: The probe below as a permanent test: stageDebounced on entity a, rerender with entity b, advance timers; expect 1 write carrying a's patch against a's base. Before: 0 writes.
evidence:
probe (renderHook, fake timers, debounceMs 100): stageDebounced({t:"typed"}) on id "a"; rerender id "b"; advance 500ms -> write calls = 0
src/hooks/useEntityCommitBuffer.ts:230-232 timer calls commitRef.current (the NEW entity's commitNow)
src/hooks/useEntityCommitBuffer.ts:184 patchFor(entityId) returns null for the old entry -> return
body:
## Summary
A debounced edit staged for record A is silently discarded when the hook re-renders with record B before the debounce fires.

## Description
The timer (src/hooks/useEntityCommitBuffer.ts:230-232) invokes the freshest commitNow, which looks up the buffer for the CURRENT entityId (src/hooks/useEntityCommitBuffer.ts:184) and returns when the entry belongs to A. The header promises "switching records cannot leak an edit" but it also cannot keep one: callers compensate today (useLevelDesignView flushes before setActiveDocId; audio editors key by record + flushOnUnmount), so the engine relies on every caller remembering. Fixed = on entityId change, commit a pending entry against the base it was staged on (store base in the entry).

## Flow
- type in a field of record A (stageDebounced)
- select record B within debounceMs from a caller that does not flush
- timer fires -> commitNow for B -> no buffer for B -> return
- A's edit is gone with no saveError

## Expected impact
Protects any future consumer that forgets the flush; current 9 consumers mostly compensate. Risk: a write against a now-unselected record must not touch B's isSaving/saveError.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a staged edit survives a record switch
Before: 0 writes after switch (probe)
After: predicted 1 write of A's patch
Method: probe - engine behaviour reproduced; the fix touches the shared engine of 9 consumers so it needs an isolated gate run
Result: better
Gate: none

title: GET /api/level-design computes a server summary the only client discards
instrument: Route test counting getDb().prepare("SELECT rooms, sync_status ...") calls per list GET: before 1, after 0; plus grep that no client reads data.summary.
evidence:
src/app/api/level-design/route.ts:28 `const summary = getSummary();` (second full-table read + JSON parse per GET)
src/hooks/useDesignDocument.ts:123 `apiFetch<{ docs: LevelDesignDocument[] }>('/api/level-design')` (summary unread)
src/hooks/useDesignDocument.ts:147 summary is derived client-side via deriveSummary
grep "api/level-design" outside src/app: only useDesignDocument.ts
body:
## Summary
Every list load re-reads and re-parses every rooms blob for a summary that the sole client ignores and re-derives itself.

## Description
The route (src/app/api/level-design/route.ts:28) runs getSummary after getAllDocs; useDesignDocument (src/hooks/useDesignDocument.ts:123) types the payload as {docs} and computes deriveSummary locally. The deriveSummary/getSummary parity is now pinned by src/__tests__/hooks/useDesignDocument.summaryParity.test.ts, so the server half can be dropped from the GET (or kept only behind ?summary=1) without losing the rule.

## Flow
- open Level Design
- GET runs getAllDocs + getSummary (2 table scans)
- client discards summary

## Expected impact
One fewer full-table read per list load (every create-less refresh). Risk: an unseen external reader of data.summary (grep found none in-tree).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one table scan per list GET instead of two
Before: 2 SELECTs over level_design_docs per GET (read path)
After: predicted 1
Method: simulation - the route is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: useFeatureVisibility copies are per-instance; a toggle misses mounted readers
instrument: Render FeatureMapTab and a VisibleSection for the same module side by side, click the section's toggle, assert the VisibleSection unmounts its children. Before: still rendered. Fix candidate: a module-level store via useSyncExternalStore + a storage event listener.
evidence:
src/hooks/useFeatureVisibility.ts:34 each instance holds its own useState copy
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/VisibleSection.tsx:14 one instance per section
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_combat/index.tsx:102-136 tabs are exclusive today, so the gap is latent in combat
body:
## Summary
Each VisibleSection reads localStorage once; a Feature Map toggle (or another browser tab) does not reach already-mounted readers.

## Description
Every hook instance owns a private copy (src/hooks/useFeatureVisibility.ts:34). In sub_combat the Feature Map and the gated panels are exclusive tabs, so a remount hides the gap; any layout that shows the map beside its sections, or a second browser tab, keeps rendering a section the user just disabled. Fixed = one shared external store per module with useSyncExternalStore.

## Flow
- mount a VisibleSection for "dps"
- disable "dps" from a FeatureMapTab mounted elsewhere
- section stays rendered until remount

## Expected impact
Latent today (exclusive tabs); prevents a confusing toggle once any surface co-mounts. Risk: re-render fan-out on toggle.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one visibility state per module
Before: N independent copies per module (one per mounted section)
After: predicted 1 shared
Method: simulation - no co-mounted surface exists in-tree to probe against
Result: better
Gate: none

title: An ok envelope without data pins every all-statuses consumer loading
instrument: Test: mockFetchRoutes all-statuses -> {success:true} (no data); mount two useFeatureStatuses consumers; assert both settle with failed=true. Before (predicted): isLoading stays true, inflight never clears for the generation.
evidence:
src/lib/api-utils.ts:88 `return ok(json.data)` (data may be undefined)
src/hooks/useFeatureStatuses.ts:119 `result.data.statuses ?? []` dereferences data
src/hooks/useFeatureStatuses.ts:149-156 `.then` clears inflight only on resolve; no catch
src/hooks/useFeatureStatuses.ts:199 `getStatuses().then(...)` no rejection path
body:
## Summary
If the all-statuses route ever answers success without data, loadStatuses throws, the shared in-flight promise rejects and is never cleared, and every consumer of that generation stays loading.

## Description
tryApiFetch returns ok(undefined) for {success:true} (src/lib/api-utils.ts:88); loadStatuses dereferences result.data.statuses (src/hooks/useFeatureStatuses.ts:119). getStatuses clears `inflight` only in its .then (src/hooks/useFeatureStatuses.ts:149), so later callers join the rejected flight (async-race-guards: removal-on-failure is the half that gets forgotten). Distinct from the recorded concurrency-guards deviation (keying of the scalar). Fixed = optional-chain data, and clear inflight in a finally.

## Flow
- route returns {success:true}
- loadStatuses throws TypeError
- inflight stays set, isLoading true for all 8 consumers until an invalidation

## Expected impact
Turns a malformed response into a visible failure instead of a permanent spinner. Risk minimal.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a malformed envelope settles as failed
Before: predicted: consumers never settle
After: predicted: failed=true, error shown
Method: simulation - not probed this round (budget); the instrument is a 20-line test
Result: better
Gate: none

title: useEntityTrackHelp has zero production consumers since the ECW deletion
instrument: Operator decision: delete the hook (+ its test, + TaskFactory.evaluateTrack / evaluate-track handler, + its context-map entry) or wire it into the current pipeline track UI.
evidence:
grep -rn "useEntityTrackHelp" src (excluding __tests__): only src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts and a comment in src/lib/catalog/catalog-module.ts:6
fb7efa5b chore(ecw): delete src/components/ecw/** (removed the consumers)
TaskFactory.evaluateTrack sole caller: src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts:52
src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts:40-45 raw fetch + `.catch(() => {})` (would need tryApiFetch if kept)
body:
## Summary
The per-track CLI evaluation hook (and the evaluate-track task it is the only dispatcher of) is unreachable from any UI.

## Description
Zero-consumer grep: no file outside src/__tests__ imports src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts; its consumers went with commit fb7efa5b. It is also the only caller of TaskFactory.evaluateTrack (src/lib/cli-task.ts:975). If kept, its refetch (src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts:40) uses raw fetch with a silent catch, against the tryApiFetch convention. Whether ECW per-track evaluation is still a wanted capability is a product call, and deletion also edits context-map.json (director-owned).

## Flow
- decide keep vs remove
- remove: delete hook + test + evaluate-track task/handler + context-map path
- keep: mount it from the pipeline track detail and switch to tryApiFetch

## Expected impact
Removes ~60 LOC + an unreachable CLI task type, or restores a lost capability. Risk: none at runtime (unreachable).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no unreachable dispatch path
Before: 0 production consumers
After: removed or 1 consumer
Method: simulation - the decision is the operator's; the grep is the evidence
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
